title: Coffee & Barista Fundamentals
description: Build coffee knowledge, professional hygiene, essential skills and a reliable café workflow.

slides.title: Welcome to Cafe de La Rue
slides.lead: Build skills through guided demonstrations, supervised practice and independent review.

facts.label: Learn actively
facts.text: Read before each demonstration. Record measurements and observations, and practice through repetition.

facts.label: Practice safely
facts.text: Ask your trainer before operating unfamiliar equipment and follow equipment-specific instructions.

facts.label: Course scope
facts.text: This internal Cafe de La Rue course is not an official TESDA assessment or government-issued qualification. Recipes are illustrative training formulas.

slides.title: Coffee & Barista Fundamentals
slides.lead: Learning objectives from the student training manual.

facts.label: Objective 1
facts.text: Describe the coffee journey and Philippine café context.

facts.label: Objective 2
facts.text: Recognize barista responsibilities, tools, and terminology.

facts.label: Objective 3
facts.text: Demonstrate professional hygiene and basic workflow.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Coffee is a brewed beverage made from roasted seeds of fruit produced by Coffea plants. A coffee cherry typically contains two seeds; the flavor of the final cup reflects farming, processing, roasting, grinding, water, and preparation.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Compare the aroma of whole beans with freshly ground coffee.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Coffee cultivation and trade developed over centuries, with roots in northeastern Africa and later widespread cultivation in Yemen and beyond. Coffeehouses became places for conversation and commerce; avoid treating popular origin legends as verified history.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Discuss how a neighborhood café can serve as a community meeting place.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Coffee moves through producers, processors, exporters, importers, roasters, distributors, and cafés. Specialty coffee places added emphasis on traceability, quality assessment, and brewing consistency, while commercial coffee serves a wide range of customers.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Trace one bag of coffee backward from café shelf to origin.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: The Philippines produces several coffee species and has diverse coffee traditions, including brewed coffee, sweetened drinks, and local specialty coffee. Café menus should respect regional preferences while explaining different roast and brewing options.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Ask a customer whether they prefer bold, sweet, or bright coffee.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Baristas prepare beverages, manage mise en place, handle orders, clean and sanitize work areas, monitor stock, and communicate with guests. Accuracy, reliability, and teamwork matter as much as drink appearance.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Repeat a sample order before starting preparation.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Core skills include dosing, grinding, extraction, milk texturing, recipe following, sensory evaluation, equipment care, and friendly service. Build consistency before increasing speed.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Prepare three identical beverages and compare their weights.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Dose is dry coffee mass; yield is brewed beverage mass; ratio compares dose to yield; extraction is dissolution of soluble material; body is perceived texture; crema is foam on espresso.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Explain dose and yield without using jargon.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Common tools include digital scales, timer, tamper, distribution tool, milk pitcher, thermometer, cleaning brush, knock box, cloths, and filtered water. Use tools appropriate to the machine and basket.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Identify which tools contact food and require routine cleaning.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Arrive in clean attire, secure long hair, keep nails short and clean, wash hands correctly, and avoid working with exposed food when ill according to workplace policy. Gloves never replace handwashing.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Demonstrate proper handwashing before touching service tools.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: A standard workflow is receive order, confirm details, prepare station, brew, assemble, verify, serve, and reset. Separate clean and dirty zones to prevent cross contamination.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Role play an order from greeting to station reset.

title: Beans, Origins & Roasting
description: Explore Philippine coffee, processing, roasting, freshness and sensory evaluation.

slides.title: Beans, Origins & Roasting
slides.lead: Learning objectives from the student training manual.

facts.label: Objective 1
facts.text: Compare four coffee species used in Philippine coffee.

facts.label: Objective 2
facts.text: Explain three major processing methods and roasting effects.

facts.label: Objective 3
facts.text: Describe storage and sensory evaluation.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Coffee beans are seeds inside coffee cherries. Green coffee is dried and prepared for roasting; roasted beans develop new aromas and are ground shortly before brewing for best control.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Examine green versus roasted coffee samples.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Arabica often offers delicate acidity and varied aromatics, while Robusta commonly provides greater bitterness, heavier body, and more caffeine by dry weight. Actual flavor depends strongly on quality and processing.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Taste two labeled samples at the same brew strength.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Liberica is known for large beans and distinctive flavor possibilities. Excelsa is commonly classified within Coffea liberica as a variety; naming conventions differ in trade. Both have relevance in Philippine coffee discussions.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Record sensory differences without ranking species as inherently good or bad.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Coffee is cultivated in regions including Benguet, Batangas, Cavite, Bukidnon, Davao, and Sultan Kudarat. Altitude, climate, farming, and processing influence quality; regional names alone do not guarantee a specific flavor.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Locate two producing regions on a map and research their harvest practices.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Ripe cherries are harvested by selective picking or stripping. Sorting removes underripe, overripe, and damaged fruit; good harvest handling helps reduce defects.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Sort a sample set of fruit images or colored tokens by ripeness.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Washed processing removes fruit material before drying, typically using depulping, fermentation or mechanical mucilage removal, washing, and controlled drying. It can emphasize clean flavor separation.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: List the main processing steps in order.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Natural coffee dries with the fruit intact; honey processing removes skin while retaining some mucilage during drying. Both require careful drying and handling to manage defects.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Compare possible fruit forward aromas without assuming every lot tastes alike.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Roasting uses heat to drive moisture loss, browning reactions, and aromatic development. Roasters track temperature, time, airflow, and bean appearance; excessive or insufficient development can affect balance.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Describe how raw and roasted coffee smell different.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Light, medium, and dark are relative descriptions rather than universal temperature standards. Lighter roasts may preserve brighter notes; darker roasts often show stronger roast derived flavors.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Compare roast appearance and aroma.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Roast development changes perceived acidity, sweetness, bitterness, solubility, and body. Brewing adjustments may be needed when switching roast profiles.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Brew a lighter and darker coffee with identical starting recipes.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Store coffee sealed, dry, away from heat, light, and strong odors. Label roast/open dates, rotate stock, and grind near service. Avoid moisture and repeated temperature swings.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Inspect labels and practice FIFO rotation.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Acidity is a bright sensory quality, not simply sourness; body is texture; sweetness balances sharpness and bitterness; aroma includes fragrance from dry grounds and brewed coffee.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Use simple descriptive words rather than unsupported tasting claims.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Taste systematically: smell dry grounds, smell brewed coffee, sip at different temperatures, record acidity, sweetness, body, finish, and defects. Cleanse palate and avoid perfume during formal tasting.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Complete a short sensory score sheet.

title: Grinders & Espresso Machines
description: Understand equipment components, grinder control, cleaning and safe operation.

slides.title: Grinders & Espresso Machines
slides.lead: Learning objectives from the student training manual.

facts.label: Objective 1
facts.text: Identify machine and grinder parts.

facts.label: Objective 2
facts.text: Explain grinder adjustments and daily care.

facts.label: Objective 3
facts.text: Apply equipment safety practices.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Espresso machines force heated water through compacted ground coffee under pressure. Stable temperature, water quality, clean equipment, and consistent puck preparation support repeatable results.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Identify the brew path from reservoir or water line to cup.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Manual lever machines require operator control; semi automatic machines let the barista start and stop brewing; automatic volumetric machines can stop at programmed volumes; super automatic units integrate more steps.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Check which controls your training machine provides.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Key components may include pump, boiler or thermoblock, heat exchanger, group head, shower screen, portafilter, steam wand, gauges, and drip tray. Designs vary.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Point to each available component on the training machine.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: The group head delivers brew water and holds the portafilter. Keep the gasket and shower screen clean; follow the manufacturer’s guidance for flushing and cleaning.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Inspect the group head only when safe to do so.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: A portafilter holds the filter basket and locks into the group. It may have spouts or a bottomless base; use the correct size and handle it carefully when hot.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Insert and remove an empty portafilter correctly.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Baskets differ in size and rated dose. Overfilling can restrict headspace and alter flow; underfilling may make preparation inconsistent. Follow basket specifications.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Check the rated dose of the installed basket.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: A steam wand injects steam to heat and texture milk. Purge briefly before and after use as instructed; wipe immediately with a dedicated clean cloth. Beware of burns.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Practice positioning a cold wand with the machine off.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Boilers, thermoblocks, sensors, and thermostats regulate water and steam temperatures. Allow warm up time and do not open pressurized or electrical housings.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Record the machine’s ready indicators.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: On demand grinders dose fresh grounds; hopper grinders store beans above burrs; single dose grinders grind measured portions. Retention and workflow differ.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Measure grinder output versus input.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Burr grinders use two cutting surfaces with adjustable spacing and typically offer better grind control than blade grinders, which chop inconsistently.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Compare ground particle consistency visually.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Finer grinds generally slow espresso flow; coarser grinds generally speed it up, with many other variables also influencing extraction. Make small adjustments and observe.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Change one setting and compare shot time.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Purge a small amount after changing settings if required, then measure a fresh dose and shot. Record adjustment direction; never force burrs together.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Write a grinder dial in log.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Scales, tampers, pitchers, brushes, cleaning tablets, and towels each have specific uses. Use approved chemicals and separate cloths for food contact and dirty areas.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Create a tool storage map.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Brush grounds, clean portafilters and baskets, wipe steam wand, empty trays, and follow manufacturer approved backflush and descaling schedules. Maintenance is not the same as daily cleaning.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Complete a cleaning checklist under supervision.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Hot metal, steam, electricity, pressurized water, wet floors, and moving grinder burrs create hazards. Turn off and isolate equipment before authorized maintenance; report leaks or damaged cords.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Identify three hazards in the training station.

rows: Delivers brew water to coffee puck

title: Espresso Extraction & Calibration
description: Measure dose and yield, dial in by taste, and document repeatable espresso recipes.

slides.title: Espresso Extraction & Calibration
slides.lead: Learning objectives from the student training manual.

facts.label: Objective 1
facts.text: Explain dose, yield, ratio, time, and flavor.

facts.label: Objective 2
facts.text: Dial in espresso using one variable changes.

facts.label: Objective 3
facts.text: Record calibration for consistent service.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Espresso is a concentrated coffee beverage prepared by forcing water through a fine, compacted bed of ground coffee. Quality depends on flavor balance and repeatability, not crema alone.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Taste a shot before deciding whether it is acceptable.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Dose is the dry coffee mass placed in the basket. Weigh it consistently; a sample 18 g dose works only if basket capacity and coffee allow.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Dose 18.0 g three times with minimal variation.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Break up clumps and level grounds before tamping to reduce uneven density and channeling. Use a consistent method and avoid losing grounds.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Compare uneven versus even preparation visually.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Apply firm, level pressure with a properly sized tamper. Repeatability and a level puck matter more than excessive force. Keep wrists in a comfortable position.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Practice a level tamp with the machine off.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Brew ratio is dose to beverage yield by mass. An 18 g dose and 36 g yield equals 1:2; ratios can be adjusted for taste and roast.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Calculate ratios for 18 g to 27 g and 18 g to 45 g.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Time is one diagnostic variable, not a universal quality score. A sample 25 to 30 seconds may be a useful starting window depending on when timing begins.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Use the same timing convention for every test shot.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Yield is the beverage mass in the cup, not the liquid volume or water added. Stop brewing at the target weight where possible.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Use a scale under the cup and record final yield.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: A shot may taste sharp, sour, thin, or salty when insufficient desirable solubles are extracted; under extraction can have multiple causes.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Compare a deliberately short yield shot with a baseline.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: A shot may taste harsh, dry, or excessively bitter when extraction is unbalanced. Bitterness can also arise from coffee and roast characteristics.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Compare a deliberately long yield shot with a baseline.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Calibration is the repeatable process of selecting dose, yield, grind, and technique, then tasting and documenting results. Keep other variables stable while testing.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Create a baseline recipe and record it.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Start with a sensible dose and ratio; pull a shot; weigh yield and record time; taste; change grind in small increments; repeat. If time is fast and flavor weak, test finer grind.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Adjust one variable at a time.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Sour and thin: check dose, yield, and grind; bitter and drying: test coarser grind or shorter yield; uneven or spraying: inspect distribution and tamping. Taste confirms whether a change helped.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Explain why time alone cannot diagnose a shot.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Check cup cleanliness, dose, yield, time, flavor, and temperature consistency. Retest when beans age, humidity changes, or grinder settings drift.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Compare opening and midday shots.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Warm up equipment, check water and cleanliness, measure baseline, pull two repeatable shots, taste, record recipe, and communicate settings to the next shift.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Sign a calibration log before service.

slides.title: A starting recipe, not a fixed standard
slides.lead: Adjust to the coffee, grinder, basket, machine, water and taste.

rows: Approximately 25–30 seconds; use a consistent timing convention

slides.title: Dose to beverage yield
slides.lead: Apply the manual’s mass-based espresso ratio.

title: Milk Steaming & Texturing
description: Practice aeration, microfoam, temperature control, pouring and safe milk handling.

slides.title: Milk Steaming & Texturing
slides.lead: Learning objectives from the student training manual.

facts.label: Objective 1
facts.text: Explain milk composition and texture.

facts.label: Objective 2
facts.text: Steam milk safely to a consistent finish.

facts.label: Objective 3
facts.text: Apply correct wand cleaning and waste controls.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Steaming heats milk and introduces controlled air to create a glossy, pourable texture. Correct technique supports sweetness perception, comfort, and milk pouring.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Observe the change from cold milk to glossy texture.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Milk contains water, proteins, fats, and lactose. Proteins help stabilize foam; fat contributes texture; temperature affects perceived sweetness and foam stability.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Compare whole and low fat milk textures.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Plant based drinks behave differently due to protein and fat composition. Use products suitable for steaming and check allergens, labels, and customer preferences.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Steam one dairy and one plant based option if available.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: A common serving target is about 55 to 65°C for dairy milk, depending on recipe and customer preference. Avoid overheating and follow ingredient guidance; use a thermometer while learning.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Record milk temperature immediately after steaming.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Start with cold milk in a clean pitcher, purge the wand safely, position the tip near the surface, introduce air briefly, then submerge slightly to form a whirlpool. Stop before the target temperature is exceeded.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Demonstrate safe wand handling.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Stretching is the early introduction of air. Listen for gentle paper tearing sounds rather than loud splashing; too much air creates coarse foam.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Compare a short and long stretching phase.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Microfoam consists of fine bubbles evenly incorporated into milk, giving a glossy wet paint appearance. Tap and swirl the pitcher gently to integrate texture.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Evaluate bubble size and surface shine.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Position the wand off center to generate a vortex, keep the tip stable, and adjust depth based on sound and movement. Different machines require different angles.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Practice with water and a drop of dish soap only for non consumable demonstrations, then clean thoroughly.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Large bubbles often mean excessive air or unstable tip position; flat milk may lack stretching; scorched flavors suggest overheating; separation occurs when milk stands too long.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Identify corrective actions for three failed pitchers.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Start with consistent espresso crema and smooth microfoam. Pour from higher to integrate milk, then lower the pitcher close to the surface to draw a simple dot or heart.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Practice a centered dot before attempting a heart.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Steam can burn skin. Keep hands clear of the tip, use pitcher handles, avoid overfilling, and never direct steam toward another person.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Point out the safe hand position.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Wipe the wand immediately with a designated clean damp cloth, purge as instructed, and follow the machine’s cleaning schedule. Never leave dried milk residue.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Perform a supervised post steam cleaning.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Measure milk based on drink size and pitcher minimums, label open containers, keep chilled ingredients cold, and avoid re steaming leftover milk for customer service.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Estimate required milk for three orders.

title: Hot & Iced Coffee Recipes
description: Prepare 16 sample training recipes with measured ingredients and service checks.

slides.title: Sample training formulas
slides.lead: All formulas are illustrative training recipes, not proprietary Cafe de La Rue formulas.

facts.label: Espresso baseline
facts.text: 18 g coffee to 36 g espresso. All ingredient quantities must be tested against actual equipment, cup capacity, ice displacement and ingredient specifications.

facts.label: Before preparation
facts.text: Confirm size, temperature, sweetness, dairy choice and allergens. Measure ingredients using a scale or calibrated measuring tool.

facts.label: Service checks
facts.text: Use fresh espresso, clean cups, safe milk handling and clean ice tools. Follow shop-approved service and labeling procedures.

slides.title: Espresso: preparation & service
slides.lead: Use a clean 90 ml demitasse; verify order and hand off promptly.

facts.label: Method
facts.text: Dose, distribute, tamp, extract to 36 g; serve immediately.

facts.label: Quality standard
facts.text: Balanced aroma, pleasant body, clean cup.

facts.label: Common mistakes
facts.text: Wrong yield; uneven puck.

slides.title: Americano: preparation & service
slides.lead: Use a clean 240 ml cup; verify order and hand off promptly.

facts.label: Method
facts.text: Add hot water to cup; pour espresso; stir if requested.

facts.label: Quality standard
facts.text: Balanced strength, comfortably hot.

facts.label: Common mistakes
facts.text: Excessive water; stale shot.

slides.title: Cappuccino: preparation & service
slides.lead: Use a clean 180 ml cup; verify order and hand off promptly.

facts.label: Method
facts.text: Extract espresso; texture milk with more foam than latte; pour promptly.

facts.label: Quality standard
facts.text: Velvety foam, integrated coffee taste.

facts.label: Common mistakes
facts.text: Dry stiff foam; overheating.

slides.title: Café Latte: preparation & service
slides.lead: Use a clean 300 ml cup; verify order and hand off promptly.

facts.label: Method
facts.text: Extract espresso; steam glossy microfoam; pour smoothly.

facts.label: Quality standard
facts.text: Silky surface, balanced milk coffee flavor.

facts.label: Common mistakes
facts.text: Large bubbles; weak coffee balance.

slides.title: Flat White: preparation & service
slides.lead: Use a clean 180 ml cup; verify order and hand off promptly.

facts.label: Method
facts.text: Extract espresso; steam fine microfoam; pour with minimal thick foam.

facts.label: Quality standard
facts.text: Smooth, coffee forward, glossy.

facts.label: Common mistakes
facts.text: Cappuccino style thick foam.

slides.title: Mocha: preparation & service
slides.lead: Use a clean 300 ml cup; verify order and hand off promptly.

facts.label: Method
facts.text: Mix chocolate sauce with espresso; add steamed milk; serve.

facts.label: Quality standard
facts.text: Fully dissolved chocolate, no separation.

facts.label: Common mistakes
facts.text: Sauce unmixed; too sweet.

slides.title: Caramel Latte: preparation & service
slides.lead: Use a clean 300 ml cup; verify order and hand off promptly.

facts.label: Method
facts.text: Mix syrup and espresso; add glossy steamed milk.

facts.label: Quality standard
facts.text: Even caramel flavor, silky texture.

facts.label: Common mistakes
facts.text: Inaccurate syrup; coarse foam.

slides.title: Spanish Latte: preparation & service
slides.lead: Use a clean 300 ml cup; verify order and hand off promptly.

facts.label: Method
facts.text: Blend condensed milk with espresso; add steamed milk; stir.

facts.label: Quality standard
facts.text: Smooth sweetness, well integrated.

facts.label: Common mistakes
facts.text: Condensed milk settled at base.

slides.title: Iced Americano: preparation & service
slides.lead: Use a clean 470 ml cup; verify order and hand off promptly.

facts.label: Method
facts.text: Add water and ice; extract espresso separately; add and serve.

facts.label: Quality standard
facts.text: Refreshing, no excessive dilution.

facts.label: Common mistakes
facts.text: Too little ice; poor strength.

slides.title: Iced Latte: preparation & service
slides.lead: Use a clean 470 ml cup; verify order and hand off promptly.

facts.label: Method
facts.text: Add milk and ice; pour espresso; stir before serving if needed.

facts.label: Quality standard
facts.text: Cold, balanced coffee and milk.

facts.label: Common mistakes
facts.text: Wrong milk measure; warm service.

slides.title: Iced Caramel Macchiato: preparation & service
slides.lead: Use a clean 470 ml cup; verify order and hand off promptly.

facts.label: Method
facts.text: Mix vanilla and milk; add ice; layer espresso; finish with caramel.

facts.label: Quality standard
facts.text: Distinct layers before stirring, balanced sweetness.

facts.label: Common mistakes
facts.text: Heavy sauce; incorrect order.

slides.title: Iced Spanish Latte: preparation & service
slides.lead: Use a clean 470 ml cup; verify order and hand off promptly.

facts.label: Method
facts.text: Dissolve condensed milk in espresso; combine with milk and ice.

facts.label: Quality standard
facts.text: No undissolved condensed milk.

facts.label: Common mistakes
facts.text: Sweetener stuck to cup bottom.

slides.title: Iced Mocha: preparation & service
slides.lead: Use a clean 470 ml cup; verify order and hand off promptly.

facts.label: Method
facts.text: Blend sauce with warm espresso; add cold milk and ice.

facts.label: Quality standard
facts.text: Chocolate evenly distributed.

facts.label: Common mistakes
facts.text: Chocolate clumps.

slides.title: Iced Vanilla Latte: preparation & service
slides.lead: Use a clean 470 ml cup; verify order and hand off promptly.

facts.label: Method
facts.text: Combine syrup and milk; add ice and espresso; stir.

facts.label: Quality standard
facts.text: Even sweetness, cold service.

facts.label: Common mistakes
facts.text: Unmeasured syrup.

slides.title: Iced Hazelnut Latte: preparation & service
slides.lead: Use a clean 470 ml cup; verify order and hand off promptly.

facts.label: Method
facts.text: Combine syrup and milk; add ice and espresso; stir.

facts.label: Quality standard
facts.text: Balanced nutty aroma; allergen label checked.

facts.label: Common mistakes
facts.text: Failure to check ingredient allergens.

slides.title: Iced White Chocolate Mocha: preparation & service
slides.lead: Use a clean 470 ml cup; verify order and hand off promptly.

facts.label: Method
facts.text: Mix sauce into warm espresso; add milk and ice; stir.

facts.label: Quality standard
facts.text: Smooth sauce dispersion, cold finish.

facts.label: Common mistakes
facts.text: Sauce not dissolved.

title: Café Operations & Service
description: Develop opening, closing, sanitation, inventory, service and teamwork routines.

slides.title: Café Operations & Service
slides.lead: Learning objectives from the student training manual.

facts.label: Objective 1
facts.text: Perform safe opening and closing routines.

facts.label: Objective 2
facts.text: Explain sanitation, storage, and FIFO.

facts.label: Objective 3
facts.text: Handle orders and complaints professionally.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Check facility safety, handwashing supplies, water, refrigeration, grinder, machine warm up, ingredients, cleaning status, cash or POS readiness, and shift assignments. Record faults before service.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Complete a signed opening checklist.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Secure ingredients, clean and sanitize food contact surfaces, perform machine specific cleaning, empty waste, reconcile records, and safely shut down equipment per manufacturer instructions.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Complete a supervised closing walk through.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Organize cups, tools, milk, syrups, clean cloths, and labeled ingredients to minimize unnecessary movement and prevent contamination.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Set up a station in a consistent order.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Wash hands before work and after contamination risks, use clean clothing, cover cuts appropriately, and follow illness reporting policy.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Demonstrate handwashing and glove changes.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Keep ingredients within supplier recommended temperature limits, minimize time outside refrigeration, use potable water and clean ice tools, and follow the café’s food safety plan.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Check and log refrigerator temperature.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Cleaning removes soils; sanitizing reduces microorganisms using approved methods. Follow label instructions for chemical concentration, contact time, and rinsing requirements.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Distinguish cleaning from sanitizing.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Label contents, preparation/opening dates, and discard dates according to product and café policy; separate allergens and chemicals from food.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Correct three intentionally incomplete labels.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: First in, first out rotates older usable stock forward. Check dates and quality before use; FIFO never overrides expiration or safety requirements.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Arrange three milk cartons by date.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Use dedicated cloths and utensils, wash hands after handling waste or money, separate allergens where possible, and never place dirty tools on clean prep areas.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Identify contamination risks in a sample workflow.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Greet promptly, speak clearly, listen, and remain respectful. A simple greeting and menu guidance help first time customers feel comfortable.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Role play a friendly first greeting.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Confirm beverage, size, hot or iced, sweetness, milk choice, and special requests. Repeat the order and clarify uncertain modifications before payment or production.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Take a complex mock order accurately.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Listen without arguing, acknowledge the concern, verify the order, offer shop approved remedies, and involve a supervisor when needed. Record recurring issues.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Role play a drink remake request.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Check recipe, appearance, cup cleanliness, drink temperature, taste where appropriate, and handoff labeling. Do not serve drinks that fail safety or quality checks.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Evaluate a staged drink before handoff.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Use clear callouts, communicate wait times, share station responsibilities, and support coworkers during rush periods without bypassing hygiene steps.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Practice order handoffs during a timed simulation.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Assign tasks by opening, during service, closing, weekly, and manufacturer maintenance intervals. Sign completed records and report incomplete work.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Create a weekly station cleaning roster.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Segregate waste according to local collection arrangements, avoid overproduction, measure beverage losses, and keep bins covered and away from clean areas.

facts.label: In practice
facts.text: Track milk waste for one practice session.

facts.label: The concept
facts.text: Be punctual, courteous, honest, safety conscious, and respectful of privacy. Follow documented workplace rules and escalate hazards immediately.
